newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares hit eighth consecutive life high.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares hit eighth consecutive life high.

text.p: The Oslo Bourse roared to another life high on Tuesday led by blue chip stock, and a dealer said there was not a cloud on the sky in the Norwegian market.
The Total index rose 0.66 percent to 915.66 points to score a life high for the eighth consecutive session. Trade was brisk at 840 million crowns.

"Everything is looking fine," a dealer said. "There is not a cloud on the sky in Norway and things continue to be upbeat in the United States." He suggested a correction could follow if the macroeconomic situation changed, for example rising interest rates in the United States.
Blue chip pulled the index up spearheaded by food-based conglomerate Orkla, which climbed 2.07 percent to 444 crowns. Consumer shares have been boosted by low interest rates recently.
"Orkla provides ideal exposure to the Scandiniavian consumer market," the dealer said.
Industrial giants Norsk Hydro, Kvaerner and Aker also closed higher.
Said another dealer: "The market is sold out. There is not a seller in sight."
